prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape 3:2, crisp voxel style, vanilla Minecraft blocks only, plain light background, no characters or animals. Two views side by side: LEFT straight-on front elevation, orthographic; RIGHT three-quarter view at the same scale. Entire building and pavement fit in both views. Skilled human builder quality: real massing, depth with proud framing and recessed openings, framed openings, roof verges/eaves/ridges, and block-built stairs, slabs, fences, trapdoors and lantern detail.

Site: A long timber market hall for a lumber wholesaler, running from one cobbled street through to the next, on pale andesite pavement, the same proud face to both streets. Building 39 wide, 30 deep, plot 43 x 38 with both pavements; 3 storeys plus twin roof gables, about 34 high to ridges. Two steep slate gables stand side by side with a valley between; a louvred vent monitor runs along each ridge. Every gable is half-timbered with dark oak posts, stepped voxel Mann-figure braces and bright white calcite daub. Down each gable centre is a stack of dark oak loading doors, one per storey. At each apex a twin-log hoist beam projects three blocks over pavement under a little hooded gable, with iron chain and a block-built hook. Two jettied storeys step out one block each over street on rows of carved stair/slab dark oak brackets. Timber store has small shuttered windows, loft has more.

Ground floor: six open counters total, three on each street between dark oak piers. North shops OAK with golden oak-log counters and oak-plank awning; SPRUCE dark brown with spruce needles; BIRCH white-barked logs and pale planks. South shops JUNGLE pinkish planks, ACACIA bright orange, DK OAK chocolate brown. Left view shows north shops; right three-quarter view shows south shops and east passage, revealing the opposite street face. Each shop has its exact name OAK, SPRUCE, BIRCH, JUNGLE, ACACIA, DK OAK in banner letters on framed fascia, an awning of its own wood stairs and trapdoors, log-end product panels on piers, hanging sign under jetty bracket. West end framed lobby on deepslate plinth, double dark oak door, lantern-lit windows. East end rounded-corner timber arch made with stairs opens to cobbled cart passage through entire building. Lantern posts at pavement corners. Small barrels, ladders and candles may furnish shop interiors.

Use these exact block ids as the material palette, preserving distinct species and vanilla textures:
frame: stripped_dark_oak_log, stripped_dark_oak_wood.
infill: calcite.
trim: dark_oak_planks, dark_oak_stairs, dark_oak_slab, dark_oak_trapdoor, dark_oak_door, dark_oak_fence, dark_oak_fence_gate.
base: cobbled_deepslate, cobbled_deepslate_stairs, cobbled_deepslate_slab.
roof: cobbled_deepslate, deepslate_tiles, polished_deepslate, deepslate_tile_stairs, polished_deepslate_stairs, deepslate_tile_slab, polished_deepslate_slab.
glass: glass_pane.
ground: polished_andesite, andesite, cobblestone.
metal: iron_chain, lantern.
shop: oak_log, stripped_oak_log, oak_planks, oak_stairs, oak_trapdoor, oak_leaves, spruce_log, stripped_spruce_log, spruce_planks, spruce_stairs, spruce_trapdoor, spruce_leaves, birch_log, stripped_birch_log, birch_planks, birch_stairs, birch_trapdoor, birch_leaves, jungle_log, stripped_jungle_log, jungle_planks, jungle_stairs, jungle_trapdoor, jungle_leaves, acacia_log, stripped_acacia_log, acacia_planks, acacia_stairs, acacia_trapdoor, acacia_leaves, dark_oak_log, stripped_dark_oak_log, dark_oak_leaves.
functional: ladder, barrel, candle.
Use vanilla banners for requested lettering and vanilla hanging signs for requested signs. No invented curved or smooth structural pieces, no custom textures, no scenery beyond plot. Focus on architecture; no palette swatch panel.
changes: Generated with the built-in image tool and saved without post-processing as concept.png in the current directory; image dimensions are 1536 x 1024.

This is raster concept art, not a block model: exact block identities, species of small foliage patches, banner base colors and concealed objects cannot be verified. Added ids are visual interpretations and practical vanilla equivalents.
The image adds apparent deepslate-brick base and verge detailing, wall-shaped lamp-post bases, slab-shaped pavement edges, and stone-brick-like pavement textures beyond the supplied palette.
Shop awnings and stock displays require additional oak_slab, spruce_slab, birch_slab, jungle_slab and acacia_slab variants.
Banner lettering, hanging signs, item-frame-like product displays and chest-like storage add objects outside the original palette. item_frame is an entity rather than a block.
Some lettering and product icons look custom-rendered rather than demonstrably achievable with vanilla banner patterns and item frames.
The hoist hooks are bespoke squared metal shapes; the supplied palette has no vanilla hook block matching them.
Loading doors read as tall continuous timber panels with hinge bands rather than clearly separate doors on every storey.
Two bracketed projecting levels are visible, but two successive full one-block storey offsets are not clearly represented.
The hoist beams' twin-log construction and exact three-block projection cannot be confirmed.
The east passage opening is square-headed rather than a clearly rounded stair-built timber arch; a continuous passage to the opposite street is not visible.
The west lobby is suggested by a narrow glazed entrance beside the shops, but its specified double door and distinct framed lobby are not clearly shown.
Shop fronts contain dense piles of timber and storage rather than six clearly delineated open counter surfaces.
The two views show opposite shop sets, but have slightly different apparent heights and cannot be confirmed as precisely the same scale.
The requested 39 x 30 building, 43 x 38 plot and approximately 34-block ridge height cannot be counted reliably from the illustration.
Some timber joins, braces, hinges and small details use finer-than-vanilla geometry or illustrative textures despite the vanilla-only constraint.
Candles remain in the planned palette but are not clearly identifiable in the image; most visible lights are lanterns.
